The recurring trigger

A similar name is a question to investigate.

Name matches need evidence, and a no-match does not establish comprehensive clearance. The proposed review log makes the source, identifiers, rationale, and reviewer visible.

Required inputs

  • Permitted counterparty identifiers
  • Dated originating source-list records
  • Supporting identity and ownership evidence

Prepared output

  • Source-linked potential-match review
  • Documented human disposition or escalation
  • Evidence references, reviewer, and timestamp

A specific review sequence

Make each step inspectable.

01

Inspect the source record

Preserve the originating list and its data-as-of date.

02

Compare identifying details

Review registration identifiers and other available evidence—not a name alone.

03

Record or escalate the disposition

Require evidence and a reason before resolving a specific match.

01 / Inside the proposed module

A disposition is an accountable decision.

The fictional reviewer compares both registration IDs and address evidence before recording a false positive for the example match.

02 / Inside the proposed module

A list has a coverage boundary.

The CSL is a screening aid focused on export restrictions. It is not a complete importer-compliance universe or a substitute for official-list diligence.

03 / Inside the proposed module

The date is part of the result.

A review based on stale list data needs another review. This preview uses a simulated list dated 01 Oct 2026, not a live feed.

Controls & scope

What the output
can—and cannot—settle.

No automated sanctions clearance. Incomplete identifiers stay unresolved or escalate. Screening requires applicable official-list, ownership, and jurisdictional diligence.

Expected reviewer: importer compliance owner and customs broker; counsel where the question requires it.

Review the limits

The pilot question

Would this help the
broker prepare the entry?

Broker-reviewed false positives and omissions, unresolved match age, and whether disposition evidence is sufficient for the selected lane.

Before the next step

Questions for this offer.

A clear boundary is part of a useful review.

All questions
Can a name match clear automatically?

No. A reviewer must inspect evidence and document a reason. Insufficient identifiers keep the match unresolved.

What does a no-match mean?

Only that no match was found in the specified sources and search at that date. It does not establish comprehensive clearance.
